title: The Kindest Man for Little Hearts
subtitle: A peaceful bedtime story about Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
blurb: A soft story about gentleness, mercy, and a heart full of light.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

Long ago…
in the city of Madinah…
there lived the kindest man.

His name was Muhammad ﷺ.

He loved Allah very much.
And Allah loved him.

He was gentle.
Very gentle.

He spoke softly.
He smiled often.
He helped everyone.

If someone was sad…
he sat with them.

If someone was hungry…
he shared his food.

If someone made a mistake…
he forgave them.

He did not shout.
He did not push.
He did not hurt.

He chose kindness.

One day, a little child came near him.

The Prophet ﷺ bent down.
He smiled.
He spoke gently.

He did not rush.

He loved children.

He would carry them.
He would greet them first.
He would make du'ā for them.

If a baby cried…
he cared.

If a child was small…
he was patient.

His heart was soft.

Very soft.

One day, a man pulled his cloak roughly.

But the Prophet ﷺ did not become angry.

He turned.
He smiled.

He answered kindly.

Because strong people are gentle.

Another day, someone was unkind to him.

But he still chose mercy.

He prayed for them.

He asked Allah to guide them.

Because his heart was full of light.

Full of mercy.

Full of love.

At night, when everyone slept…

The Prophet ﷺ would stand and pray.

Quietly.

Softly.

He thanked Allah.

He asked Allah to forgive his people.

He asked Allah to protect children.

He asked Allah to guide hearts.

He cared for everyone.

Even us.

Yes… even you.

The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah is Gentle.

And he showed us how to be gentle too.

So when we share…
we are following him.

When we forgive…
we are following him.

When we speak softly…
we are following him.

Now imagine him smiling.

A calm smile.

A kind smile.

A warm smile.

His heart was peaceful.

And when we remember him…
our hearts feel peaceful too.

Your body feels calm now.

Your hands are resting.

Your eyes are soft.

Just like the Prophet ﷺ was gentle…

You can be gentle.

Just like he forgave…

You can forgive.

Just like he trusted Allah…

You can trust Allah.

Allah loves kind hearts.

Very much.

Breathe slowly…

In…
and out…

In…
and out…

Sleep with a gentle heart.

Sleep with kindness.

Allah is watching over you.

And we say,

Allahumma salli wa sallim
'ala Muhammad ﷺ.

🌙 Ameen.

title: Prophet Ibrahim and the Quiet Stars
subtitle: A calm bedtime story inspired by the Qur'an
blurb: Stars, moon, and sun fade — but Allah never disappears.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

Long ago…
in a quiet land…
there was a kind man.

His name was Ibrahim.

Ibrahim loved Allah very much.
He wanted to know his Lord.
He wanted to worship the One who made everything.

One night…
Ibrahim looked up at the sky.

The sky was dark.
Very dark.
Very calm.

And in the sky…
there were stars.

Small stars.
Bright stars.

Twinkling.

Ibrahim looked at a bright star.
It shone beautifully.

He wondered,
"Is this my Lord?"

But then…

The star slowly faded.

It disappeared.

Ibrahim said gently,
"I do not love things that disappear."

The night stayed quiet.

Then the moon rose.

Big.
Round.
Glowing softly.

Ibrahim looked at the moon.

It lit up the sky.

He wondered,
"Is this my Lord?"

But later…

The moon went down.

Slowly.
Quietly.

It disappeared too.

Ibrahim said softly,
"I do not love things that go away."

Then the sun rose.

Bright.
Warm.
Very big.

It filled the sky with light.

Ibrahim saw how strong it was.

But when evening came…

The sun also went away.

It set.
It disappeared.

And Ibrahim understood something very important.

The stars disappear.
The moon disappears.
The sun disappears.

But Allah…

Allah never disappears.

Allah is always there.

Always watching.
Always caring.
Always near.

Allah made the stars.
Allah made the moon.
Allah made the sun.

Allah made the sky.
Allah made the earth.
Allah made you.

Ibrahim felt peaceful in his heart.

Very peaceful.

He said,

"I turn my face to the One
who made the heavens and the earth."

He chose Allah.

The One who stays.

The One who never leaves.

The One who never sleeps.

Now imagine the sky at night…

Dark.
Calm.
Full of tiny stars.

The stars twinkle softly.

Twinkle…
twinkle…

The moon glows gently.

The night is quiet.

Allah is watching over you.

Just like He watched over Ibrahim.

The stars may fade.
The moon may go down.
The sun may set.

But Allah is always there.

Your body feels heavy now.

Your eyes feel soft.

The sky is calm.

The night is gentle.

Allah is near.

Breathe slowly…

In…
and out…

In…
and out…

Rest now.

Sleep peacefully under Allah's beautiful sky.

🌙 Ameen.

title: Prophet Nuh and the Safe Ark
subtitle: A peaceful bedtime story inspired by the Qur'an
blurb: A rocking ark, soft rain, and trusting Allah when the world feels big.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

Long ago…
in a quiet land…
there lived a good man.

His name was Nuh.

Nuh loved Allah.
He listened to Allah.
He told people to be kind…
to be good…
to worship Allah alone.

But many people did not listen.

Nuh felt sad sometimes.
But he kept trusting Allah.

One day…
Allah gave Nuh a special job.

Allah told him,
"Build an ark."

An ark is a very big boat.
A strong boat.
A safe boat.

So Nuh began to build.

Knock…
knock…
knock…

The wood was strong.
The ark was big.

Bigger…
and bigger…

Nuh worked slowly.
Carefully.
Patiently.

Because when Allah gives a job…
we do it calmly.

Soon…
the ark was ready.

Allah told Nuh,
"Bring your family.
Bring the believers.
Bring two of every animal."

And so they came.

Two by two.

Two little birds.
Two soft sheep.
Two tall camels.

Step…
step…
step…

The animals walked calmly inside.

The sky grew cloudy.
The wind began to blow.

Soft at first.

Then stronger.

The rain began to fall.

Drip…
drop…

Drip…
drop…

The rain fell more.

And more.

The ground became water.
The water became deep.

But inside the ark…
it was safe.

Very safe.

The ark began to float.

Slowly…

Up…
and down…

Up…
and down…

Like a cradle.

Like when someone rocks you to sleep.

The rain fell outside.

But inside…

It was calm.

The animals rested.
The people rested.

Nuh trusted Allah.

Because Allah promised safety.

The ark floated gently.

Up…
and down…

Up…
and down…

No rushing.
No fear.

Just trust.

Days passed.

The rain became softer.
Then lighter.
Then quiet.

The water slowly went down.

Down…
and down…

The ark rested on a mountain.

The sky became clear.
The air felt fresh.

Allah had protected them.

Allah had kept His promise.

Nuh looked around and said,

"Alhamdulillah."

Because when Allah protects us…
we say thank You.

And what is our lesson?

When the world feels big…
Allah is bigger.

When the rain feels heavy…
Allah is in control.

When we feel unsure…
we trust Allah.

Just like Nuh in the ark.

Now imagine the ark floating gently…

Up…
and down…

Up…
and down…

Your body feels heavy.

Your eyes feel soft.

The rain is quiet now.

The sky is calm.

Allah is watching over you.

Allah is protecting you.

Rest now.

Sleep peacefully.

Like the ark…
safe…
and calm…
on the water.

🌙 Ameen.

title: Baby Musa and Allah's Gentle Plan
subtitle: A peaceful nap story inspired by the Qur'an
blurb: A little basket on a gentle river — Allah’s plan is soft and sure.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

Long ago…
in a faraway land…
there was a tiny baby.

His name was Musa.

Baby Musa had a loving mama.
She held him close.
She kissed his soft head.
She loved him very, very much.

But the land was not safe.
There was a mean ruler.
He was not kind.

Mama Musa felt worried.
Very worried.

But Allah spoke to her heart.

Allah made her heart calm.

Allah gave her an idea.

Allah told her,
"Do not be afraid.
I am with you."

So Mama Musa made a little basket.
A soft basket.
A safe basket.

She placed baby Musa inside.

The river was flowing gently.

Not fast.
Not wild.

Gentle.

Mama Musa kissed him.

She whispered,
"Allah will protect you."

She put the basket on the river.

The water carried the basket.

Slowly…
gently…
up…
and down…

Up…
and down…

Baby Musa was not afraid.

Because Allah was watching.

Allah always watches.

The river moved softly.
The basket rocked gently.

Rock…
and rock…

Like when someone rocks you to sleep.

The sun was warm.
The sky was quiet.

Allah guided the basket.

Not too far.
Not too fast.

Just where it needed to go.

The basket reached a beautiful garden.
A palace garden.

A kind woman found the basket.

She looked inside.

"Oh," she said softly.
"A baby."

Her heart felt love.

Allah put love in her heart.

She picked up baby Musa gently.

Very gently.

She held him close.

And baby Musa was safe.

Allah protected him.

Allah protected his mama too.

And do you know something special?

Allah brought baby Musa back to his own mama.
So she could hold him again.

Because Allah keeps His promises.

Always.

And what is our lesson?

When we feel scared…
Allah is with us.

When mama feels worried…
Allah is with her.

When babies sleep…
Allah watches over them.

Just like baby Musa in the basket.

The river moved slowly…

Up…
and down…

Up…
and down…

Your breathing is slow now…

In…
and out…

In…
and out…

Allah is watching over you.

Allah is protecting you.

Just like baby Musa.

Rest now.

Close your eyes.

The river is gentle.
The night is calm.
Allah is near.

🌙 Ameen.

title: The Prophet Who Remembered Allah
subtitle: A gentle nap story inspired by Prophet Yunus عليه السلام
blurb: When hearts feel tired, remembering Allah brings calm.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

Long ago, there was a good man.
His name was Yunus.

Yunus loved Allah.
He told people about Allah.
He wanted everyone to be kind.

But one day…
Yunus felt sad.

Very sad.

The people were not listening.
They were not being kind.

Yunus felt tired in his heart.

So he went on a boat.
A big boat.
On the big sea.

The sea was calm at first.
Very calm.

But then the wind came.
Whoooosh…

The waves grew big.
Up…
and down…

The boat rocked.

The people were afraid.

And Yunus went into the water.

Splash.

But listen carefully…

Allah was watching.

Allah always watches.

A big whale came.
A very big whale.

The whale did not hurt Yunus.
No.

The whale kept Yunus safe inside.

It was dark inside the whale.
Very dark.

Quiet.
Very quiet.

Yunus was alone.

But he was not alone.

Because Allah was there.

Yunus remembered something important.

When we feel sad…
When we feel tired…
When things are hard…

We remember Allah.

Yunus whispered softly,

"La ilaha illa Anta,
Subhanaka,
Inni kuntu minaz-zalimeen."

(There is no god but You.
You are perfect.
I made a mistake.)

He whispered it slowly.
Softly.
Again and again.

And Allah heard him.

Allah always hears.

The whale swam gently.
Up…
and down…

Up…
and down…

Yunus felt calm.

Very calm.

Because when we remember Allah…
our hearts become peaceful.

Soon…
Allah told the whale to bring Yunus back.

The whale came to the shore.

The sun was warm.
The sand was soft.

Yunus rested.

Allah forgave him.
Allah helped him.
Allah was kind to him.

And Yunus learned something very important:

When we feel sad…
We remember Allah.

When we feel tired…
We remember Allah.

When we make mistakes…
We say sorry to Allah.

And Allah is Most Merciful.

Very Merciful.

Very Kind.

Now it is nap time.

Your body feels heavy.
Your eyes feel soft.

If you ever feel sad…
If you ever feel tired…

You can whisper:

"La ilaha illa Anta…"

Allah hears you.

Allah loves you.

Now breathe slowly…

In…
and out…

In…
and out…

Rest now.

Allah is watching over you.

🌙 Ameen.

title: Eesa and the Quiet Builder Truck
subtitle: A Little Light nap story
blurb: After a day of helping, Eesa and his builder truck slow down together.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

The building yard was quiet.
No hammering.
No lifting.
No noise.

Eesa's builder truck was parked neatly.
He had worked all day.
He carried sand.
He helped fix a path.
He waited patiently when others needed a turn.

Now his wheels felt heavy.
Very heavy.

Little Eesa walked slowly to the truck.
He sat beside him.
He stayed close.

"Good job today," Eesa whispered.
"Alhamdulillah for strong wheels."

The truck made a soft sound.
Like a sleepy sigh.

"But my engine is still awake," the truck said.

Eesa nodded gently.
"That's okay," he said.
"We will slow it down."

Eesa took a deep breath.

In…
and out…

Again…

In…
and out…

The truck listened.
His engine slowed.
Lower…
and lower…

The moon shone above them.
The night breeze was cool and calm.

"Allah gives us strength," Eesa whispered.
"And Allah gives us rest."

One light turned off.
Then the other.

The wheels stopped turning.
The engine became quiet.

Very quiet.

The yard felt peaceful.
Nothing to build.
Nothing to fix.

Eesa whispered softly,
"Bismillah."

The truck felt warm.
Safe.
Heavy with sleep.

His breathing was slow…
and calm…
and steady…

Soon…
very soon…
the builder truck was fast asleep.

Ameen.

title: Eesa and the Kind Helpers
subtitle: A Little Light nap story
blurb: Friendly helper animals learn that even helpers need quiet rest.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

The sun had gone to sleep.
The sky was dark and gentle.
The town was quiet.
Very quiet.

The kind helpers were back home.
A soft little cat.
A careful bird.
A sleepy puppy with kind eyes.

They had helped all day.
They carried.
They listened.
They shared.
They were kind.

Now their paws and wings felt heavy.
Their eyes felt soft.

Little Eesa walked slowly into the room.
He walked softly.
He spoke softly.

"Alhamdulillah," Eesa whispered,
"you helped so many people today."

The puppy stretched.
A long stretch.
Then a yawn.

The cat lay down.
Slowly.
Carefully.

"But I'm still awake," the bird whispered.

Eesa smiled kindly.
"That's okay," he said.
"Even helpers take time to rest."

Eesa sat on the floor.
He stayed very still.

He took a slow breath.

In…
and out…

Again…

In…
and out…

The helpers watched.
They breathed too.

The lights were low.
The beds were warm.
No rushing.
No noise.

"Allah is watching over us," Eesa whispered.
"We are safe."

The puppy closed his eyes.
The cat curled up.
The bird tucked her head.

The room felt calm.
Very calm.

Eesa whispered again,
"Alhamdulillah for rest.
Alhamdulillah for sleep."

Their breathing became slow…
and slower…
and slower…

Nothing to do.
Nowhere to go.
Just rest.

Soon…
very soon…
all the kind helpers were fast asleep.

Ameen.

title: Nuri and the Quiet Kitchen
subtitle: A Little Light nap story
blurb: Nuri the night lantern helps the kitchen settle into soft sleep.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

The kitchen was quiet.
Very quiet.

The lights were low.
The floor was still.
Nothing was moving.

It was nap time.

On the shelf glowed Nuri.
Nuri was a little night lantern.
Her light was soft today.
Not bright.
Not busy.

Soft.

Nuri looked around and whispered,
"Alhamdulillah."

Carrot was nearby.
Carrot was tired.
Very tired.

Tomato sat still.
No rolling.
No bouncing.

Broccoli did not wiggle.
Not even a little.

Everyone had done enough for today.

Nuri spoke very gently,
"No cooking now.
No rushing now.
Now we rest."

She turned her glow down lower.

Click.

Quiet mode.

The kitchen felt calm.
Safe.
Peaceful.

Nuri settled slowly.
Very slowly.
She did not rush.

She took a deep breath.

In…
and out…

Again…

In…
and out…

The vegetables listened.
They breathed slowly too.

Carrot lay down.
Tomato closed his eyes.
Broccoli became very still.

Nuri whispered again,
"Allah is watching over us.
Allah keeps us safe."

The fridge hummed softly.
The clock ticked slowly.

Tick…
tick…

Nothing to do.
Nowhere to go.

Nuri rested her light against the shelf.
Her glow felt warm.
Just right.

She whispered,
"Alhamdulillah for rest.
Alhamdulillah for quiet."

The vegetables' breathing was slow…
and slow…
and slow…

The kitchen stayed quiet.
Very quiet.

No noise.
No trouble.
Only rest.

Nuri closed her eyes.
Her light grew softer.
Comfortably soft.

The vegetables slept.
Nuri slept.

Everything slept.

Soon…
very soon…
the whole kitchen was resting.

Ameen.

title: Prophet Yusuf and the Quiet Patience
subtitle: A gentle bedtime story inspired by the Qur'an
blurb: A soft story about waiting calmly and trusting Allah's plan.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

Long ago…
there was a kind boy.

His name was Yusuf.

Yusuf had a soft heart.
He loved his father.
He loved Allah.

One day…
things felt hard.

Very hard.

Yusuf was far from home.
He felt alone.
He felt small.

But listen carefully…

Allah was with him.

Allah always is.

Yusuf did not shout.
He did not rush.
He waited.

Patiently.
Quietly.
Gently.

Days passed.
Nights passed.

Yusuf remembered Allah.
He whispered soft words.
He kept a kind heart.

Even when he felt sad…
he chose patience.

Even when he felt unsure…
he trusted Allah.

Because Allah’s plan is gentle.
Even when we cannot see it yet.

Later…
Allah made a way.

A good way.
A kind way.

Yusuf was safe.
Yusuf was cared for.
Yusuf’s heart felt peaceful.

Alhamdulillah.

And what is our lesson?

When we wait…
we can wait with soft hearts.

When we feel far…
Allah is near.

When we do not understand…
Allah understands.

Just like Yusuf.

Now breathe slowly…

In…
and out…

In…
and out…

Your body feels heavy.
Your eyes feel soft.

Allah is watching over you.
Allah’s plan is kind.

Rest now.
Sleep with a patient heart.

🌙 Ameen.

title: Prophet Sulayman and the Soft Voices
subtitle: A calm story about kindness to animals
blurb: Listening gently — to ants, birds, and quiet hearts.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

Long ago…
there was a wise man.

His name was Sulayman.

Sulayman loved Allah.
Allah gave him a special gift.

He could understand
the soft voices of animals.

One day…
Sulayman walked with his people.

The sun was warm.
The path was quiet.

Then Sulayman heard something tiny.

Tiny feet.
Tiny whispers.

Ants.

The ants were talking softly.

“Be careful…
walk gently…”

Sulayman smiled.
He listened.

He did not laugh.
He did not rush past.

He cared.

He told his people,
“Let us be careful.
Let us be kind.”

Because even little creatures
matter to Allah.

Birds sang above him.
Soft songs.
Gentle songs.

Sulayman listened to them too.

He thanked Allah
for every living thing.

Big things.
Small things.
Quiet things.

And what is our lesson?

We can listen.
We can walk softly.
We can be kind to animals.
We can be kind to people.

Just like Sulayman.

Now the birds are quiet.
The ants are resting.
The path is calm.

Your breathing is slow…

In…
and out…

In…
and out…

Allah made the birds.
Allah made the ants.
Allah made you.

Rest now.
Sleep with a gentle heart.

🌙 Ameen.

title: Eesa and the Rainy Window
subtitle: A Little Light nap story
blurb: Soft rain on the glass helps Eesa slow down for sleep.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

The afternoon was grey and soft.
Not dark.
Not bright.

Soft.

Little Eesa sat by the window.
His knees were tucked in.
His blanket was warm.

Outside…
the rain began.

Drip…
drop…

Drip…
drop…

The rain tapped the glass.
Gently.
Again and again.

Eesa whispered,
“Alhamdulillah for rain.”

The trees swayed slowly.
The street was quiet.
Cars moved like sleepy snails.

Eesa’s eyes felt heavy.
But his mind still wanted to play.

So he watched one raindrop.
Just one.

It slid down the window.
Slowly…
slowly…

Eesa breathed with it.

In…
and out…

Another drop.
Another breath.

In…
and out…

“Allah sends the rain,”
Eesa whispered.
“Allah sends rest too.”

The room felt peaceful.
No rushing.
No noise.

Only rain.
Only breath.
Only calm.

Soon…
very soon…
Eesa’s eyes closed.

The rain kept singing softly.
And Eesa slept.

Ameen.

title: Nuri and the Quiet Moon Walk
subtitle: A Little Light nap story
blurb: Nuri imagines a gentle moon walk — then settles into sleep.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

Night came quietly.
The house was still.
The lights were low.

Nuri the night lantern glowed softly.
Not bright.
Just enough.

She whispered,
“Bismillah.”

Tonight Nuri imagined a walk.
A quiet moon walk.
No shoes rushing.
No loud steps.

Just soft light
and soft sky.

In her mind…
she stepped outside.

Step…
step…

The moon was round.
The stars were tiny.
The air was cool.

Nuri looked up and said,
“Subhanallah.
Allah made this beautiful sky.”

She walked a little more.
Then she stopped.

She did not need to go far.
Imagining was enough.

She breathed.

In…
and out…

In…
and out…

The moon felt close.
The night felt safe.
Allah was near.

Nuri turned her glow down lower.

“Time to rest,”
she whispered.
“Alhamdulillah for the moon.
Alhamdulillah for sleep.”

Her light became warm and small.
Her thoughts became quiet.

Soon…
very soon…
Nuri was sleeping.
And the quiet moon watched over the night.

Ameen.

title: The Bowl of Shared Dates
subtitle: A Little Light kind-habits story
blurb: Sharing food and saying Alhamdulillah with a happy heart.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

In a small kitchen
sat a little bowl.

Inside the bowl
were soft brown dates.

Sweet.
Simple.
Ready to share.

Little Eesa looked at the bowl.
His tummy felt hungry.
His hands wanted them all.

But then he remembered.

Sharing is kind.
Sharing is light.

Eesa picked up one date.
He gave it to Mama.

“For you,”
he said softly.

Mama smiled.
“JazakAllahu khayran.”

Eesa gave one to his little sister.
She giggled.
He felt warm inside.

Then Eesa took one for himself.

He said,
“Alhamdulillah.”

Thank You, Allah,
for food.
Thank You for family.
Thank You for enough.

The dates were not many.
But the kindness was big.

Very big.

And what is our lesson?

When we share…
our hearts feel bigger.
When we say Alhamdulillah…
our hearts feel peaceful.

Now the bowl is empty.
The kitchen is quiet.
Tummies are happy.

Breathe slowly…

In…
and out…

Rest with a thankful heart.

Ameen.

title: Gentle Hands, Soft Words
subtitle: A Little Light kind-habits story
blurb: Using soft hands and soft words at home.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

At home
there are many things to touch.

Toys.
Books.
Doors.
People we love.

Little Eesa looked at his hands.

“These hands can be gentle,”
he whispered.

He closed a door softly.
Click.

Not bang.
Soft.

He picked up a book carefully.
He passed a cup with two hands.
He patted the cat like a feather.

Soft hands.

Then Mama asked for help.
Eesa wanted to say something fast.
Something loud.

But he took a breath.

In…
and out…

“Yes, Mama,”
he said softly.

Soft words.

When his sister bumped his block tower…
Eesa felt a little storm inside.

Then he remembered.

Gentle hands.
Soft words.

“It’s okay,”
he said.
“We can build again.”

The storm became a cloud.
Then the cloud floated away.

Allah loves gentle hearts.
Allah loves kind voices.

Now the house feels calm.
The toys are resting.
The voices are quiet.

Your hands are resting too.

Breathe…

In…
and out…

Sleep with gentle hands.
Sleep with soft words.

Ameen.

title: Bismillah in the Morning Light
subtitle: A Little Light kind-habits story
blurb: Starting the day calmly with Bismillah — not loud, just gentle.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

Morning came softly.
Golden light on the wall.
Birds outside.
A new day.

Little Eesa opened his eyes.
He did not jump up.
He did not shout.

He stretched slowly.

Then he whispered,

“Bismillah.”

In the name of Allah.

A quiet beginning.
A kind beginning.

He sat up.
He smiled at Mama.
He put on his socks one foot at a time.

No rushing.
No loud morning.

Just Bismillah
before water.
Bismillah
before breakfast.
Bismillah
before play.

Each word was small.
But it made the day feel gentle.

Mama said,
“What a peaceful start.”

Eesa nodded.

“Allah is with us
in the morning too.”

And what is our lesson?

We can begin softly.
We can remember Allah early.
We can make mornings calm.

Now imagine morning light…
warm…
quiet…
slow…

Even if it is night where you are…
your heart can rest
with Bismillah.

Breathe…

In…
and out…

Rest now.
Allah is near.

Ameen.

title: Sorry and a Soft Hug
subtitle: A Little Light kind-habits story
blurb: Saying sorry and making peace with a gentle hug.
text:
Bismillah 🌙

Sometimes hearts bump.
Sometimes words come out too fast.
Sometimes toys get snatched.

Little Eesa took his sister’s crayon.
He did not mean to make her sad.
But her eyes looked watery.

Eesa felt a squeeze in his chest.

He remembered something important.

When we make a mistake…
we can make peace.

He took a slow breath.

In…
and out…

He walked over softly.

“I’m sorry,”
Eesa said.

Not loud.
Not grumpy.
Soft.

“I won’t take it again.”

His sister sniffed.
Then she nodded.

Eesa opened his arms.
She stepped in.
A soft hug.
A warm hug.
A peace hug.

“Alhamdulillah,”
Mama whispered from the door.
“That is a kind heart.”

The crayons were shared.
The room felt light again.

And what is our lesson?

Sorry can be soft.
Hugs can heal little hurts.
Allah loves those who make peace.

Now the crayons are resting.
The hug is remembered.
The house is calm.

Your body feels heavy…

In…
and out…

Sleep with a peaceful heart.

Ameen.
